stories.notes: Complex live-preview feature spanning three environments (GO, UP, MX) with no acceptance criteria and null spec. openspec must first elaborate AC and add technical depth (preview rendering, state sync, CMS integration, multi-env considerations). speckit then hardens with testability criteria, security checks (XSS in preview iframe, auth for preview endpoints), and edge cases (concurrent edits, stale previews, network failures).

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a novel capability — no live_preview config exists in the Stack initialization. The attachment point is the contentstack.Stack() call in src/services/contentstack.ts where the live_preview object must be added. Downstream consumers (useContent, ContentstackLink, ContentstackImage, ContentstackTable, ContentstackContentCards, etc.) all flow through this pipeline and must not regress. VCs are derived solely from the description since ACs are empty. Contentstack hosts are unreachable at test time, so VCs verify our code's configuration and request behavior, not the remote service's response.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all ACs are original to this review. Criteria were derived from the story title ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), the identified files (contentstack.ts, useContent.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, contentCard.ts), and openspec's notes about the Stack() attachment point and downstream consumers. Key areas covered: (1) Stack config inclusion (AC-1), (2) preview parameter propagation through the query pipeline (AC-2), (3) no-regression guarantee for non-preview mode (AC-3), (4) graceful fallback on invalid/missing tokens (AC-4), (5) security — no token leakage to client bundles (AC-5), (6) feature toggle support (AC-6), (7) downstream component rendering of preview content (AC-7), (8) all three codebases (AC-8), (9) content type and locale respect in preview (AC-9), (10) correct preview host routing (AC-10). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I was unable to read the actual source files, so these ACs are based on standard Contentstack Live Preview SDK patterns and the file paths/names provided. The exact field names, parameter shapes, and integration points may need adjustment once the source code is reviewed. In particular, AC-5 (token leakage) and AC-6 (feature toggle) assume patterns common to Next.js/Contentstack setups but the actual env-var names and config structure may differ.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. Openspec identified the technical attachment point (the contentstack.Stack() call in src/services/contentstack.ts) and traced the downstream consumer pipeline (useContent, ContentstackLink, etc.), establishing architectural context and noting that Contentstack hosts are unreachable at test time so VCs must verify code configuration rather than remote responses. Speckit hardened this with 10 testable acceptance criteria covering config inclusion, parameter propagation, no-regression guarantees, graceful fallback on invalid tokens, security (token leakage to client bundles), feature toggle support, and multi-codeline coverage. The five verificationCriteria are observable and map directly to the described behavior (draft content display, real-time updates, non-preview regression). The declared file set (contentstack.ts, useContent.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, contentCard.ts) is plausible for a live-preview pipeline spanning config-to-render. All manifest paths verified as exact matches across gotransit, upexpress, and metrolinx codelines — no missing paths. Brownfield ticket correctly shows empty acceptanceCriteria with acceptanceChanged=false from both agents. Speckit's caveat about not reading source files is noted but does not lower the score per policy. Ordinary open questions around exact env-var names and config structure are within a competent writer's resolution scope.
